So corporate social responsibility is the attempt on the part of companies to manage their business and processes so as to generate some kind of positive impact.

In fact, companies nowadays are increasingly asked to consider the effect of their economic activities on different categories of stakeholders, such as customers, suppliers, shareholders, communities, and ultimately, the environment.

Some companies even go beyond their legal obligations in terms of environment protection and public well-being by implementing CSR policies because they are aware that this will represent an important advantage for their business.
By investing in CSR, companies improve their reputation and their public image.

And this is a win-win strategy because, in this day and age, consumers' shopping decisions are markedly influenced by the engagement that a company has in certain causes, namely social and environmental causes.

Since they are increasingly conscious of social and environmental issues, they prefer to buy goods and services from brands that are actively engaged in creating a positive impact with their activities.
